item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Josh Hart has now been praising the Memphis Grizzlies following their solid start to the 2026/27 season. The Grizzlies have so far played nine NBA games this term and have a 6-3 record. Ty Jerome has been one of their standout players during the early stages of the campaign and he was singled out by Hart when he was discussing Memphis. When appearing on the Roommates Show , Hart was asked: “Have any teams early on surprised you guys?” He responded: “Memphis, Ty Jerome too. He’s averaging like 40 or whatever. But this is why you don’t put too much stock in it, I’m not saying he’s not hooping, but nobody in the NBA will average 40 this season. “There will be ebbs and flows, some guys are shooting 74% from three. Are they going to shoot 74% from three all season? No, but granted, Ty is.” The Grizzlies’ last game saw them face off with the Oklahoma City Thunder in the NBA Cup on Friday night. They lost that tie 128-97 and will now turn their attention back towards the normal NBA season matches. Memphis are next in league action on Monday evening when they will face the Toronto Raptors, who are 5-4 at present. item.title: “Don’t See the Dodgers Shelling Out a Long-Term Mega Contract for Tarik Skubal” – Dodgers Insider Explains Why Kyle Tucker-like Deal Is The Way to Go
item.description: Tarik Skubal - LA Dodgers | © Imagn The Athletic’s Katie Woo discussed Tarik Skubal’s free agency and how the 2025 World Series champions could land the two-time AL Cy Young winner despite competition from other suitors. On the Foul Territory podcast, Woo explained how the team’s president of baseball operations, Andrew Friedman, has negotiated short-term contracts since last offseason, offering clues about the kind of deal Skubal might receive. She said it could be similar to the contract Kyle Tucker signed last season. “I don’t see the Dodgers shelling out a long-term mega contract for Tarik Skubal for the same reasons they didn’t do for Kyle Tucker. Andrew Friedman wants to prolong that team’s competitive window, and the Dodgers over the last year or so have strayed from those mega contracts,” Woo said. “But they are able, if they continue to operate as currently constructed, to really ramp up the AAV. So could we see a similar structure to what the Dodgers offered Kyle Tucker, a shorter term, four or five years, and a much higher AAV as their option? That’s certainly the thought process going into the GM meetings,” she added. Tucker was awarded a staggering four-year, $240 million contract by LA last offseason as the team aimed to bolster their roster in an attempt at a three-peat; however, they fell short at the NLCS. Skubal went 12-7 in 2026, splitting the season between the Tigers and LA. He was 1-1 in the postseason, starting the opening games of the NLDS and NLCS. He finished with a 2.72 ERA, 186 strikeouts, and a 0.96 WHIP. Although his stats fell short of those he posted over the previous two years in Detroit, Skubal still had a strong season, leading analysts to believe he could command one of the highest pitching contracts in MLB history this offseason. ESPN’s Buster Olney on Tarik Skubal’s free agency On his podcast Baseball Tonight , ESPN’s Buster Olney said Skubal could be given a short-term contract along the lines of what was offered to Kyle Tucker last offseason. “I had one agent predict to me that they are gonna kind of do… It’s going to be more Kyle Tucker-type structure, like six times 60, which would set a record by far,” Olney said. While LA remains in the running to sign Skubal this offseason, big-spending teams such as the Yankees, Mets, Phillies, and Padres, along with potential dark horses like the Tigers, White Sox, and Angels, are also pursuing the generational talent represented by super agent Scott Boras. item.title: ‘No s***, Sherlock’: Michael Vaughan takes brutal dig as Usman Khawaja reopens Australia's ball-tampering scandal
item.description: Former England captain Michael Vaughan has reacted sarcastically to the fresh revelations surrounding Australia's infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, suggesting that Usman Khawaja's claims about widespread knowledge within the team were hardly surprising. Khawaja has reignited the 'Sandpapergate' controversy through excerpts from his upcoming autobiography, claiming that discussions about tampering with the ball were much more widespread during Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa than Cricket Australia's investigation had established. Taking to X, Vaughan took a dig at the revelations, suggesting that the latest claims merely confirmed what many had suspected all along. He also questioned why the issue was being revisited nearly eight years after the scandal and called for everyone to move on. "So we finally now know the most hidden secret in the game … all the Aussie team knew about the sandpaper … 8 yrs later it all comes out … no shit Sherlock … now can we just move on …" Vaughan posted. The controversy dates back to the third Test between Australia and South Africa in Cape Town in March 2018, when Cameron Bancroft was caught using sandpaper to rough up the ball. The incident triggered a major crisis for Australian cricket and resulted in lengthy suspensions for Steve Smith, David Warner and Bancroft. Cricket Australia's investigation at the time concluded that prior knowledge of the ball-tampering plan was limited to the three players. Head coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of direct involvement but resigned shortly after the series. However, Khawaja has now claimed that conversations about roughing up the ball, including through the use of sandpaper, took place openly within the team. "It was all of us," the former Australia batter said in his autobiography, according to the Sydney Morning Herald. Khawaja, who was cleared of wrongdoing during the original investigation, also described the conversations as "open, lighthearted discussions" and maintained that awareness of the subject extended beyond just the batters, bowlers or coaching staff. Cricket Australia has stood by its original investigation, insisting that all relevant information presented to the governing body had been considered. It also maintained that individuals still had the opportunity to provide any additional information. Australia captain Pat Cummins, who featured in the Cape Town Test, had earlier played down suggestions that Khawaja's autobiography would trigger further fallout from the scandal. Australia and South Africa have since faced each other again in a Test series, with the visitors returning to the country last month for the first time since the 2018 controversy. item.title: Fascinating stats! How often your Bundesliga club plays in prime time
item.description: Fascinating stats! How often your Bundesliga club plays in prime time As of Thursday, exact kickoff times have been set for every match in the first half of the Bundesliga season. That means we can now say precisely how often each team will play at which times and, most importantly, on which days. A glance at the figures makes one thing immediately clear: "smaller" clubs play far more often at 3:30 p.m. on Saturday afternoons—the traditional Bundesliga prime-time slot—than the country's big, historic clubs. It is no coincidence that Paderborn (14) and Elversberg (11), two newly promoted sides without much top-flight history, feature in the top three of the Saturday crowd. The reason—apart from some clubs' involvement in European competitions—is obvious: teams that do not generate huge TV interest are much easier to "hide" in the simultaneous-match coverage than in standalone broadcasts. The simultaneous-match format, with its many goals and dramatic twists, remains as popular as ever, while a standalone match between, say, Paderborn and Elversberg would presumably attract far less interest. Clubs like Bayern Munich are the losers in this development—or, more precisely, their fans are. Bayern will play on a Saturday afternoon just three times during the first half of the season, and not once at home. item.title: I disagree’ – Jason Kidd defends Giannis Antetokounmpo after Doc Rivers call out
item.description: Photo by Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto via Getty Images Following Doc Rivers’ comments about Giannis Antetokounmpo, another one of his former coaches, Jason Kidd, has come to his defence. Doc Rivers was Giannis Antetokounmpo’s head coach with the Milwaukee Bucks for a few years, but they weren’t able to achieve much success together. The head coach went on record this week suggesting that Giannis’ style of play makes him difficult to coach and manage. The Greek Freak isn’t having the best start to his Miami Heat career, and this Rivers’ criticism naturally led to media dialogue. While some agreed on Doc’s takes about Antetokounmpo trying to force plays instead of playing within the system, Jason Kidd defended the superstar. Jason Kidd says that going downhill is Giannis Antetokounmpo’s ‘superpower’ and what opens up his game Kidd coached Giannis in Milwaukee from 2014 to 2018 and played a major role in his development. He helped him improve as a ball-handler and encouraged him to attack the basket. The two had a good relationship, and the two-time MVP even offered to speak to the Bucks’ ownership to try to save his job. Kidd is still backing his former star, too, strongly disagreeing with what Rivers had to say about Antetokounmpo. “I don’t,” Kidd said on ESPN when asked about whether he shares Doc’s views. “I think when you talk about stars, they are hard to coach but they want to be coached. Giannis’ superpower is to get downhill and he makes plays. “Doc saying that it’s his IQ, I disagree with that. Giannis understands how to play the game. His forcefulness, getting downhill, that’s what it’s all about. When he causes a problem, he’s one of the top 5 players in the league.” Considering all the wild takes floating around about him, Antetokounmpo will be grateful to Kidd for his words defending him. The noise is often amplified when a star is going through a rough patch, too. If the Heat figure things out and start winning, all the Giannis criticism will quiet down once again. item.title: “We Were Gonna Foul”: Matt Painter Reveals Exact Moment Where Purdue Lost the Game as Valparaiso Upset Boilermakers
item.description: Purdue Boilermakers head coach Matt Painter. © IMAGN Matt Painter pinpointed exactly where his No. 24 Purdue Boilermakers lost the 83-80 double-overtime game against the unranked Valparaiso Beacons on Friday in West Lafayette. Justus McNair won the game for Valparaiso with a buzzer-beating 3-pointer, but there was one moment when Purdue could have won. In his post-game conference, Painter revealed the painful moment came at the end of first overtime, when Purdue failed to secure a defensive rebound after intentionally fouling Chaney. After that, the Beacons guard hit a buzzer-beating shot from deep, sending the game into second overtime. Painter said the Boilermakers should have fouled Chaney instead of letting him take that 3-point shot. “You gotta be able to get that rebound,” Painter said. “You gotta be able to squeeze that and chase that ball down and give it to Chaney. Give Chaney credit. He went and got the ball; he had the wherewithal to get behind the line and obviously make that shot. So yeah, it was not something that we discussed, right? We were gonna foul. We weren’t gonna let them make that three.” After taking a 70-67 lead with 6.8 seconds remaining in the first overtime, the Boilermakers intentionally fouled Rakim Chaney. After Chaney missed the free throw, the Boilermakers should have hustled for the rebound. But even after that, the next best option would have been to foul Chaney. But the Boilermakers failed to seize the moment as Chaney paved the way for the Beacons to win in second overtime. “Fabulous” Rakim Chaney Shines in Purdue’s Upsetting Valparaiso Loss In the second overtime, Purdue’s Daniel Jacobsen tied the score at 80-80 with just 4.4 seconds remaining. Once again, Purdue may have played it too casually as Valparaiso guard Justus McNair raced down the floor within a couple of seconds. Just before time expired, McNair shot from deep and nailed the basket for the buzzer-beating 83-80 finish. For the Beacons, Rakim Chaney had a spectacular outing, finishing with 35 points, eight rebounds and six assists. Painter also praised Chaney’s performance, calling it “fabulous.” “But everything we were worried about was Chaney; I thought he was fabulous.” The loss dropped Purdue to 0-2 for the first time since the 1976-77 season. Their winning streak against Missouri Valley Conference opponents also ended, with their previous defeat to a Missouri Valley opponent coming in 1978, per Reuters . For now, Painter will talk with his team about the game and identify moments when they could have gained an advantage so such losses don’t happen again. item.title: Zinedine Zidane says Mbappe can play in his preferred position for France – “There will no problem”
item.description: Zinedine Zidane says Mbappe can play in his preferred position for France – “There will no problem” The second international break of the season is just around the corner, with France’s new manager Zinedine Zidane recently releasing his final squad. France are slated to take on Italy and Turkiye as part of the UEFA Nations League campaign. Les Bleus are already topping the group with three wins in four matches. France’s latest squad includes four Real Madrid players in Aurelien Tchouameni, Ibrahima Konate, Eduardo Camavinga and Kylian Mbappe. Zidane on Mbappe’s position There has been some speculation on how Zidane will implement Mbappe into this team. Last time out, the new coach simply did not get enough time with the Real Madrid star, who picked up an injury in the win over Turkiye. Mbappe could operate as a left winger for France. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) This time around, Mbappe will be available and when asked about his integration to the team, Zidane has stated clearly that the forward will have the freedom to operate in his preferred position. “Kylian Mbappe can play in several positions, but he will also be able to play in his preferred position,” he said (h/t RMC Sport ). “Perhaps during this break, during these matches. So that means up front, there will be no issue,” he added. A positive for Real Madrid? Zidane’s comments effectively suggest Mbappe might be given the opportunity to operate in his preferred left-wing position. All eyes on Mbappe this international break (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) This could be interesting for Mbappe but not so much for Real Madrid, as Los Blancos would prefer the Frenchman continue to lead the frontline. That is because Real Madrid still lack the services of a proper alternative for Mbappe in the number nine position, as Endrick and Carlos Espi have yet to prove themselves as a trusted starting candidate for Jose Mourinho. It will, nonetheless, be interesting to see how Mbappe operates as a left winger for France, should Real Madrid eventually look to move on from Vinicius Jr and sign a new forward in the future.

item.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, all set to captain Bihar in Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy as selectors look for fresh direction
item.description: KOLKATA: At 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is set for his first assignment as Bihar’s senior team captain, with the selectors handing the teenage batting sensation the reins for the upcoming Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. The move underlines their faith in his leadership potential as Bihar seek a turnaround after losing all four of their opening Ranji Trophy matches. Sakibul Gani led Bihar in the first three Ranji games before Mangal Mahrour took over against Goa, but neither captain could arrest the slide. The BCCI-appointed selection committee, headed by Harvinder Singh, has now turned to Vaibhav, with Suraj Kashyap named his deputy for the domestic T20 tournament. The decision by the selection committee, led by chief selector Harvinder Singh and comprising Amitabh Vijayvargiya and S Sarath, marks another significant step in Vaibhav’s rapid rise. Having represented Rajasthan Royals in the IPL and made his India debut in T20Is, the teenager has quickly established himself as one of the country’s most exciting batting prospects. His recent international exploits included a 45 off 19 balls against New Zealand in the third T20I, where he shared a record-breaking opening stand with Abhishek Sharma. Vaibhav has also had a taste of leadership at the zonal level. Named vice-captain of the Ishan Kishan-led East Zone side, he briefly took charge during the Duleep Trophy semifinal when Kishan left the field with a finger injury. During that spell, he also successfully executed a DRS call. However, his rapid elevation to positions of responsibility comes amid questions about the need to balance expectations with his development. Sachin Tendulkar recently advocated giving Vaibhav more opportunities in red-ball cricket to help him grow as a complete cricketer, while cautioning against placing excessive responsibility on his young shoulders too early. The selectors, though, appear to have a different assessment, with the Bihar captaincy adding another responsibility to Vaibhav’s expanding portfolio. BCA president Harsh Vardhan said the appointment would provide the youngster another opportunity to develop as a leader. “Vaibhav has already demonstrated tremendous talent, confidence and maturity at a young age, and this responsibility will provide him with another opportunity to grow as a cricketer and leader,” he said. Bihar begin their SMAT campaign in Indore on Nov 14. The 17-member squad also includes Mahrour and Sunrisers Hyderabad pacer Shakib Hussain, whose availability will depend on fitness assessments after the first two matches. Singh and Vijayvargiya will be present in Indore to watch Bihar’s matches. item.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following NBA Cup loss to Cavaliers
item.description: CLEVELAND -- The Philadelphia 76ers paid a visit to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Friday and it didn't go well as they fell 119-95 on the road. The loss drops Philadelphia to 1-1 in Group B play for the NBA Cup and the blowout loss will hurt its overall point differential in the standings. Jaylen Brown had 20 points, five rebounds, and five assists for Philadelphia, VJ Edgecombe had 19 points and four steals, and Tyrese Maxey added 17 points and four assists. LeBron James had eight points, three assists, and seven rebounds. Joel Embiid shot 0-for-9 for six points. Here are the three biggest takeaways for the Sixers following the loss: James' turnovers and poor spacing The Sixers fell behind by 15 in the opening quarter as they couldn't take care of the ball. James committed two of his six turnovers on the night in the first quarter and Philadelphia just had a tough time finding any rhythm. Philadelphia shot just 30% in the first quarter and 2-for-9 from deep as the Cavaliers opened up a big lead. The cause of the turnovers was a number of different things, but the Sixers didn't have the proper spacing in this one as Philadelphia had a tough time finding any open looks. "Yeah, I mean, I think that it certainly didn't help us," coach Nick Nurse said of the poor spacing. "I think there was either—I mean, I think officially it was only two turnovers, but could have been four. I guess they gave Jo shot attempts on a couple of those that he might have got hit on the sweep up. I guess they gave those shot attempts, but yeah, we just got off to a poor start with taking care of the ball, and that hurts because I think (Donovan) Mitchell's first eight points were in transition, right? You got all these game plans and everything, and he's going to be aggressive. You hate to kind of gift him eight out of the blocks like that, and our poor offensive execution was a result of that." Embiid's shooting struggles and poor spacing Embiid shot 0-for-9, and some of that is on him, but the Cavaliers really pushed up on him and didn't give him much space to operate out on the floor. item.title: Arsenal youth trains with first-team amid senior international call-up
item.description: Arsenal youth trains with first-team amid senior international call-up Arsenal youngster James Scanlon is having a good week, receiving call-ups to train with the Gunners first-team and to play with Gibraltar over the international break. Photo via Scanlon on Instagram Ahead of Arsenal’s game against Hull City on Saturday, 20-year-old winger James Scanlon was spotted training with Mikel Arteta’s senior side on Friday. Arsenal are obviously a little low on wingers at the moment, with Bukayo Saka out of action through injury and Max Dowman suspended. With Scanlon scoring three goals and assisting one in his first five Premier League 2 appearances for the Gunners, he’s earned a chance in training. But that wasn’t the only boost for the former Manchester United winger this week, as he’s also been called up to the Gibraltar senior squad for the November break. Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images The international call-up isn’t surprising, as Scanlon has already made 28 appearances for Gibraltar in his young career. In fact, Scanlon is currently the team’s second-top scorer of all time, with six goals. He only trails retired international Liam Walker , who scored eight during his international career. The Arsenal man will get an opportunity to add to his total in Nations League fixtures away to Andorra and at home to Malta over the upcoming break. Photo by Carsten Harz/Getty Images With all that being said, it’s unlikely Scanlon receives a call-up for the Arsenal first-team squad for Saturday afternoon’s match against Hull City. Though Arsenal are a little light in forward areas, Saka and Dowman are actually the only players in the entire senior squad expected to miss the game. Three times they went to Wembley, twice winning the FA Trophy, in 1972 and 1979, under the command of Roy Chapman, father of Leeds United title winner and former Stoke City striker Lee.
